questions.q: What is the main difference between symmetric and asymmetric encryption?
o: Symmetric uses one shared key; asymmetric uses a key pair
Symmetric encryption is always slower than asymmetric
Asymmetric encryption works without any keys at all
Symmetric keys can encrypt data but never decrypt it
questions.w: Symmetric (AES) is fast and used for bulk data. Asymmetric (RSA, ECC) solves key exchange and signatures but is slower.

questions.q: How does HTTPS (TLS) typically combine the two?
o: Asymmetric crypto agrees a session key, then AES protects the data
TLS uses only RSA to encrypt every byte of the traffic
TLS uses AES with a key that is hard-coded in the browser
TLS hashes all traffic so that nobody can read the content
questions.w: The handshake authenticates the server and derives a shared session key. The bulk traffic then uses a symmetric cipher.

questions.q: Which is the right tool to check that a downloaded file was not tampered with, when you have a trusted published value?
o: A cryptographic hash such as SHA-256
Symmetric encryption with a shared key
Base64 encoding of the downloaded file
Compression of the file before download
questions.w: A hash gives a fixed fingerprint. Any change to the input changes it. Base64 is only an encoding, not security.

questions.q: A digital signature is created with which key, and verified with which?
o: Signed with the sender's private key, checked with the public key
Signed with the public key, checked with the private key
Signed and checked with one shared secret value
Signed with the receiver's private key and public key
questions.w: Only the owner holds the private key, so a valid signature proves origin and integrity. Anyone can verify with the public key.

questions.q: What is a salt in password hashing?
o: A random per-password value mixed in before hashing
A secret key shared by every user of the system
A second hash applied on top of the first hash
An encryption key kept in the user's browser
questions.w: Salts are not secret. They make identical passwords hash differently and break precomputed rainbow tables.

questions.q: Why must a nonce or IV never be reused with the same key in AES-GCM?
o: Reuse can leak message relationships and break authentication
Reuse makes the encryption noticeably slower for large files
Reuse makes the nonce grow larger than the size of the key
Reuse makes the cipher refuse to start until it is restarted
questions.w: GCM nonce reuse is catastrophic: an attacker can recover the authentication key and forge messages. Use a fresh random or counter nonce each time.

questions.q: What does a certificate authority (CA) provide in public-key infrastructure?
o: A signed statement binding a public key to an identity
The private key belonging to each website
A mechanism that makes the TLS handshake faster
A free allowance of bandwidth for secure sites
questions.w: Browsers trust a set of root CAs. A server certificate chains up to one of them, so clients know the key belongs to that domain.

questions.q: Which statement about hashing versus encryption is true?
o: Hashing is one-way, encryption can be reversed with the key
Both hashing and encryption can be reversed freely
Hashing can be reversed only with a secret key
Encryption is one-way and cannot be reversed
questions.w: Use hashing for passwords and integrity. Use encryption when you must recover the original data.
